plausible: The tests were failing intermittently and I wanted to investigate that first.
The dependency update introduced an unexpected regression.
A flaky test blocked the pipeline and I was waiting for a clean run.
The type checker found an issue I needed to understand before pushing.
I was reproducing the bug locally so the fix would actually stick.
The code review comments needed a proper response, not a quick patch.
I hit a merge conflict and was resolving it carefully.
The formatter and the linter disagreed, so I stopped to sort that out.
I was writing a regression test before changing the behaviour.
The stack trace pointed at a library I had not touched, so I traced it.
questionable: Git did something weird.
It worked on my machine until I looked at it.
The diff was bigger than I expected, so I left it for a clearer head.
I was going to push, and then the terminal scrolled.
The branch name made sense yesterday.
I rebased, and the commits rearranged themselves.
The IDE suggested a change and I trusted it for a moment.
I closed the laptop to think, and the thought left with the screen.
The function was only supposed to be a temporary helper.
I was waiting for the compiler to finish feeling ready.
absurd: A cosmic ray flipped a bit in the dependency lock file.
The semicolon unionised and refused to terminate the statement.
The stack overflowed because the stack was on a tea break.
A parenthesis wandered off and has not checked back in.
The unit tests achieved sentience and demanded better names.
The linter developed opinions about my variable names and walked out.
The binary was compiled under a contradictory moon.
An off-by-one error escaped and is living in the hallway.
The debugger stepped into a function that does not exist yet.
The source file was last edited by a very confident ghost.
unhinged: The production server became self-aware and rejected the pull request.
The code compiled out of spite and then immediately uncompiled.
My editor filed a counter-pull-request against me.
The garbage collector collected my motivation and refused to return it.
The repository asked to be left alone and I respected its boundaries.
A recursive function called me back and we are still on the line.
The type system declared my idea illegal in three jurisdictions.
The commit message wrote itself and then asked for a co-author credit.
The tests passed so hard they broke the concept of failure.
I asked the code what it wanted and it requested a new career.

plausible: The deployment pipeline was red and I did not want to stack another change on it.
A certificate was close to expiry and I rotated it before it became an incident.
The staging environment did not match production, so I paused to check why.
A health check was flapping and I was watching it settle.
Disk usage on the build agent crossed the threshold we agreed to act on.
I was waiting for the container registry to finish a slow push.
An alert fired for a service I own, so that came first.
The rollback plan was incomplete and I did not want to ship without it.
A secrets rotation was in progress and deploys were frozen on purpose.
The load balancer config needed a review before the next traffic shift.
questionable: Docker was having a day.
The pod restarted and I decided that counted as progress.
Kubernetes rescheduled the problem onto a different node.
I cleared the cache, which felt like a strategy.
The pipeline failed on a step nobody admits to owning.
Helm rendered something, and I chose not to read all of it.
The container was healthy if you did not ask it any questions.
I restarted the service and called that an investigation.
The volume mounted, emotionally, somewhere else.
Terraform wanted to destroy something and I looked away politely.
absurd: The cluster achieved consensus that my deploy was a bad idea.
DNS propagated into a neighbouring dimension.
The container escaped, saw the office, and climbed back in.
YAML indentation formed a crop circle in the manifest.
The load balancer started load-balancing blame.
A sidecar container developed a personality and a grudge.
The health check passed because it was too polite to fail.
Prometheus graphed my confidence and the line went straight down.
The ingress tried to ingress and got lost in the lobby.
The replica set replicated the outage for high availability.
unhinged: The orchestrator orchestrated a coup and I was not on the new chart.
The pods formed a union and are refusing to schedule my feelings.
Docker composed a symphony and will not run anything else.
The service mesh became an actual mesh and trapped the request.
CI discovered free will and declined the job.
The canary deploy was an actual canary and it had notes.
Kubernetes apologised and then deleted the namespace anyway.
The rollback rolled forward out of artistic conviction.
Our uptime objective was interpreted by the cluster as a suggestion from a stranger.
The production namespace filed for independent statehood.

plausible: The meeting ran long and I lost the block I had set aside for the change.
I was writing up the decision so we would not have to meet about it again.
A stakeholder asked for a clarification and I answered that first.
The action items from yesterday were still open and I was closing them.
I was pulled into an incident review that overlapped the work.
The calendar invite moved and took my focus with it.
I needed a decision from the meeting before the code would be worth writing.
Notes from the design discussion contradicted the ticket, so I checked.
I was preparing the demo so the review would be about the work, not the setup.
Two meetings were booked on top of each other and I attended the one I owned.
questionable: The meeting could have been an email, and then it was both.
I nodded at the right times and that used up the hour.
We agreed to take it offline, which is where it stayed.
Someone shared their screen and the rest of the day left the chat.
The agenda was optimistic and I matched its energy by doing nothing.
I was waiting for the recording so I could attend it later, allegedly.
The parking lot of topics became a multi-storey car park.
My camera was off, and so was the part of me that writes code.
We circled back so many times I am still in orbit.
The action item was assigned to everyone, which meant I assumed someone else.
absurd: The meeting invited itself and refused to leave.
A whiteboard marker achieved quorum and voted to extend.
The conference phone joined from a previous decade and filibustered.
We action-itemed the concept of time and it was deferred.
The slide deck presented us, and we were underprepared.
A breakout room broke out and has not been recaptured.
The mute button muted the entire sprint.
Calendar holds started holding each other.
The standup stood up and walked out of the building.
Minutes were taken so thoroughly they took the afternoon too.
unhinged: The recurring meeting became self-aware and scheduled a meeting about that.
I attended the meeting's meeting and we still have no notes.
The agenda filed a grievance against linear time.
Zoom asked me who I was and I did not have a strong answer.
The shared document edited the attendees.
We reached alignment, and alignment reached back.
The facilitator facilitated my disappearance from the ticket.
A status update updated my status to legendary and absent.
The icebreaker never thawed and we are still in it.
The meeting ended, but only in a legal sense.

plausible: The estimate did not include the review cycle, so the date slipped honestly.
A higher-priority fix landed in the same window and I switched to that.
I found a defect that would have shipped if I had rushed the last step.
The acceptance criteria changed after the work was already sized.
I was waiting on a dependency from another team that is still open.
The original date assumed no interruptions, and there were interruptions.
Testing took longer because the edge cases in the ticket were real.
I cut scope rather than pretend the full change would fit.
A release freeze started before I could merge.
I flagged the risk last week and this is the risk arriving.
questionable: The deadline and I have agreed to see other people.
I was on track until the track moved.
It is basically done, which is a kind of done.
I scheduled the work for future me, and future me is furious.
The date was more of a vibe.
I would have finished if the day had contained more day.
The ticket says urgent, and so did the other six.
I saved it for the last responsible moment, and the moment left.
Progress was made in a direction.
The burndown chart burned down my confidence instead.
absurd: The deadline moved into next week to find itself.
Timezones ganged up and stole Thursday.
The Gantt chart developed a hole and the milestone fell through.
A calendar reminder reminded me of a different life.
The sprint tried to sprint and pulled a hamstring.
The due date was printed in invisible ink.
Story points were denominated in a currency that collapsed.
The timeline folded and Tuesday is now after Friday.
My estimate was correct for a planet with longer afternoons.
The clock on the wall is in a union and stopped for negotiations.
unhinged: The deadline looked at the ticket and resigned.
I finished it tomorrow, which has not happened yet, so we are fine.
Chronology filed a bug and I am waiting on that release.
The date picker picked a fight.
I delivered the work to last week and they sent it back unopened.
The milestone achieved escape velocity.
Time asked for a status update and I asked time to wait.
The schedule is a haunted house and I do not go in after lunch.
We shipped the concept of the feature, which is more than some teams.
The deadline was a social construct and I am between constructs.

plausible: A delivery arrived and someone had to be home for it.
The washing machine finished and the laundry needed to come out before it sat.
A repair visit was booked in a window I could not move.
I had to collect a prescription before the pharmacy closed.
School called and I needed to deal with that before coming back to the keyboard.
The kitchen leak got worse and waiting would have made it a bigger job.
I was cooking because nobody else was going to, and the food had a timer.
A neighbour needed help with something that could not wait until evening.
The bins go out on a schedule and I missed the last chance yesterday.
I had a household appointment that was booked before this work was.
questionable: The dishwasher and I entered a negotiation.
I sat down to start and the house presented a list.
Something in the fridge required a moral decision.
I was going to work, and then I noticed the floor.
The kettle boiled and that became the plan.
A lightbulb died and replacing it took the precise length of the task.
I alphabetised a drawer and called it admin.
The cat occupied the chair with a mandate.
I went to find a pen and emerged an hour later with a different pen.
The laundry multiplied while I was looking for a matching sock.
absurd: The hoover unionised and is refusing soft furnishings.
A houseplant requested a one-to-one about lighting.
The toaster produced a ticket instead of toast.
Dust formed a committee and tabled the afternoon.
The fridge magnet demagnetised my intentions.
A sock escaped to the shadow realm behind the dryer.
The thermostat developed opinions and none of them were mine.
The recycling sorted me into the wrong bin.
A spider held the doorway and had the better argument.
The kettle whistled in a frequency that cancelled productivity.
unhinged: The house asked who I was and I did not have building access.
Furniture rearranged itself into a maze with no laptop at the centre.
The washing machine completed a cycle and also my career.
I opened a cupboard and a smaller deadline fell out.
The doorbell rang from the inside.
A roomba mapped my excuses and is now charging on them.
The lights dimmed whenever I opened the editor.
The cutlery drawer staged an intervention.
I tried to leave for my desk and the hallway was longer than yesterday.
The smoke alarm tested itself, and then tested me.

plausible: I was context-switching between two tasks and lost the thread of this one.
I needed a short break so the next hour of work would be accurate.
Something personal came up and I dealt with it before it got bigger.
I misread the priority and spent the time on the item above this one.
I was waiting for an answer I needed before I could continue.
The instructions were ambiguous and I stopped rather than guess wrong.
I wrote down what I had learned so far so it would not live only in my head.
A smaller task turned out to have a real blocker.
I ran out of the uninterrupted time the change actually needs.
I picked it up late enough that starting would have meant stopping badly.
questionable: I was about to start, and then I became philosophical.
The task and I are in a situationship.
I did research, if you count staring.
Motivation updated its terms of service and I have not accepted them.
I put it on a list, and the list is in a very safe place.
I was busy being almost ready.
The idea was clear until I tried to have it.
I scheduled deep work and then dug a very shallow hole.
Focus was installed but not running.
I gave it my second-best hour, which did not show up.
absurd: Productivity was lost in the same drawer as the good cables.
A thought required a firmware update and bricked.
The day was delivered to the wrong address.
My attention span filed for remote work and did not connect.
A small task put on a coat and became a large task.
The to-do list to-did something else.
Motivation left a note that said back in five, several eras ago.
I opened a new tab and fell into a gentle abyss.
The clock hands are clapping slowly.
Competence took a personal day and left me the keys.
unhinged: I became the person this task was waiting on, and I do not pick up.
Reality submitted a pull request removing this afternoon.
I attempted the task in a mirror dimension and it shipped there.
The void replied to my status update with a read receipt.
I have done it in every timeline except this one.
Free will clocked out and middle management has no comment.
The task looked at me and we both apologised.
I outsourced it to tomorrow and tomorrow is a shell company.
Existence returned a 500 and asked me to retry never.

plausible: I was mentally already in the weekend.
This looked much easier at 14:00.
Nobody should have approved a pull request this late on a Friday.
I did not want to start a change I could not finish before people left.
The reviewer I needed had already signed off for the week.
Shipping this after 16:00 would have meant owning it all weekend.
I wrapped up loose notes so Monday would not start from zero.
The Friday deploy window had already closed.
I used the last hour to write down where I stopped.
A Friday afternoon change has burned us before, so I waited.
questionable: It was Friday, and the keyboard knew.
I opened the ticket, saw the time, and closed it like a professional.
My best thinking had already left for the weekend.
I was present in body and in a soft out-of-office reply.
The change can wait until the week has been replaced.
I did a Friday amount of work, which is a recognised unit.
Slack went quiet and I took that as a sign from the universe.
I would have done it if it had been a Tuesday problem.
The commit would have been haunted by Monday.
I protected production from myself, which should count.
absurd: The weekend sent a cease and desist.
Friday afternoon code is legally fiction.
My laptop entered weekend mode and greyed out the repository.
The sun set on the sprint in a literal and binding way.
A seagull stole the last useful thought.
The office plants clocked out and I followed their lead.
Time became syrup sometime after lunch.
The pull request looked at the clock and asked to be excused.
Friday compiled with warnings and I ignored them on principle.
The calendar marked the day complete while I was still in it.
unhinged: The week ended without consulting me and I respect its authority.
I merged with the weekend and the conflict is unresolved.
Saturday has already started in my heart and it has no CI.
The ticket was last seen heading west at speed.
I told the code we would talk on Monday and the code seemed relieved.
Friday achieved finality and there is no appeal.
My remaining focus left in a group chat I am not in.
The repository is closed for the season.
I attempted work and the day returned HTTP 451.
Monday can have this. Friday has union rules.
